## Line 1

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/brep.library.plato, line 1](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/brep.library.plato#L1).

```plato
//==
// # B-rep
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - BREP shell operations
//  - BREP primitive shells
//  - BREP tessellation

library Brep
{
    //==
    // # BREP shell operations
    //
    // Evaluation, topology queries, validation, and deformation for the edge-use
    // shell declared in `brep.types.plato`. IGeometry dispatch is an exhaustive `match`
    // over the `BrepCurve` / `BrepSurface` sums, so adding a curved case is a new
    // arm in each function here, not a new field anywhere.
    //
    // Deform is the faceted decay: it moves the CONTROL points (vertices, segment
    // endpoints, patch corners) through the mapping and rebuilds each sum case
    // from them, so straight edges stay straight and a warped Planar face decays
    // to the Bilinear case through its four UV corners. The exact
    // function-composition deform of the C# sketch needs function-valued payloads
    // that these sums intentionally do not carry.

    //==
    // IGeometry evaluation

    // The point at parameter t (0 at Start, 1 at End) along an edge curve.
    Eval(c: BrepCurve, t: Number): Point3D =>
        match (c) {
            Line(segment) => segment.PointAt(t);
        };
```

```plato
    // The point at a unit-square UV parameter on a face surface.
    Eval(s: BrepSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D =>
        match (s) {
            Planar(patch) => patch.Eval(uv);
            Bilinear(patch) => patch.Eval(uv);
        };
```
